title: The Tower of the Comedy: Milan, the Plate, and the Two Lighthouses
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Brera, the Politecnico, and the Port

stops.name: Milan, the carpenter's second son
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by en.wikipedia and it.wikipedia, 'Mario Palanti', which agree on 20 September 1885
stops.campa: In Milan a second son is born to Giovanni Palanti, a carpenter, and Virginia De Gasperi, a dressmaker. The family comes out of the province of Cremona and has settled among the city trades. The elder brother, Giuseppe, is already turning toward paint and will make his name among the Divisionists and the poster designers of Milan. Mario is given the same city and the same academy, and will spend his working life on the far side of the Atlantic, raising towers for other men's fathers in a language he learns after twenty-four.
suggested_refs: The Brera district of Milan, birthplace and training ground of both Palanti brothers
Giuseppe Palanti's Divisionist posters, the family's other career

stops.name: Accademia di Brera, the painter's training
stops.date_confidence: contradiction, recorded and not resolved: it.wikipedia dates the entry to 1904, es.wikipedia to 1905. Both give his age as nineteen, which fits 1904 or 1905 depending on the month, and neither gives a month or day; both are defaulted to 01 January
stops.campa: At nineteen he enters the Accademia di Brera to study painting, in rooms his brother already knows. He is taught figure and shadow first, and ornament, and how a story is carried across a wall by relief; the arithmetic of loads comes later and elsewhere. The buildings he will raise on the Rio de la Plata are read by their sculpture before anyone reads their plan: telamones straining under balconies, Latin cut into vaults, a beacon where a spire would go. He does not finish as a painter. Giuseppe keeps that trade, and Mario crosses the city to the Politecnico.
suggested_refs: The Accademia di Brera painting course, c. 1904-1905

stops.name: Politecnico di Milano, the architect's diploma
stops.date_confidence: year attested by it.wikipedia, which dates the architecture degree to 1909, the same year as the departure for Argentina; month and day unknown and defaulted to 01 January. The teaching address of the architecture school in those years is given by no reachable source, so the pin is the generic Milan coordinate and stands for the city, not the building
stops.campa: He takes the second training at the Politecnico's school of architecture and graduates an architect. Milan in these years is building its own eclectic century, historicist facades over steel and reinforced concrete, and the school teaches both halves without embarrassment. In the same year the diploma is signed he accepts work in a country he has never seen, on a pavilion for an exposition that has not opened, in a city where a hundred thousand Italians a year are coming ashore. He does not live in Italy again for twenty-one years.
suggested_refs: The Politecnico di Milano school of architecture before its move to Piazza Leonardo da Vinci

stops.name: Genoa, the emigrant port
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, not attestation: the 1909 departure for Argentina is attested by en.wikipedia and es.wikipedia, but no reachable source names a port, a vessel, or a sailing date. Genoa is the standard emigrant port for northern Italy in that year and stands here as a reconstructed stop; month and day defaulted to 01 January
stops.campa: He goes down to Genoa, the mouth through which northern Italy empties itself into the Americas, and takes ship for the River Plate. No manifest, no vessel, no sailing date survives him; he leaves Italy the way half a million others leave it that decade, as a name on a list nobody kept. He is twenty-four, an architect of one year's standing, with a commission waiting and no Spanish. Behind him the Brera, the Politecnico, the carpenter's house. Ahead a continent building faster than Europe and paying better for it.
suggested_refs: The 1909 emigration route from Genoa to the River Plate, reconstructed and not documented for Palanti

stops.name: Brussels, the gold medal
stops.date_confidence: placement, not attestation: en.wikipedia records a gold medal at an International Exhibition in Brussels and gives no year at all. 1910 is placed on the Brussels Exposition Universelle, the obvious candidate, and the placement collides with his documented presence in Buenos Aires that year. The collision is recorded and not resolved; the stop is ordered after the 1909 departure so that the segment reads in date order, which does not make the year attested
stops.campa: At an international exhibition in Brussels the young architect is given a gold medal. It is the only European honour of his early career that any reachable source records, and no source dates it either. Whether he is in Belgium at all in the year the Exposition Universelle opens is unestablished: that summer he is documented in Buenos Aires. The Belgian capital sees him once and does not keep him. Every later prize he takes comes from clients whose fathers sailed out of Genoa and Naples as he has just done.
suggested_refs: The Brussels Exposition Universelle of 1910, the likeliest but unconfirmed occasion of the medal

stops.name: Puerto Madero, the landing
stops.date_confidence: year attested by en.wikipedia and es.wikipedia; month and day unknown and defaulted to 01 January. The pin is the Puerto Madero docks as the port of entry, distinct from the canonical central Buenos Aires pin used elsewhere in this journey
stops.campa: He comes ashore at Buenos Aires in the year before the centenary, into a port working at full stretch: grain out, Italians in, the new docks of Puerto Madero not fifteen years old. The city he enters is the richest in the southern hemisphere and is spending like it. Its Italian merchant families, Costaguta and Roccatagliata and Uboldi and Barolo, want facades that say Milan and Genoa, and there is almost nobody here to draw them. Alberto Gerchunoff, brought over from Russia as a boy, is writing this same port into Spanish in the same years.
suggested_refs: The Puerto Madero docks, completed 1897, gateway of the Italian arrival

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the studio of Prins and Ranzenhofer
stops.date_confidence: the employment is attested by es.wikipedia and it.wikipedia; no source gives a start month, an end date, or an address. The research pool's span of 1909-1914 and its phrase 'for five years' are inventions and have been dropped. The coordinate is the canonical Buenos Aires pin inherited byte-identically from victoria_ocampo.journey.json and stands for the city, not for an office
stops.campa: He goes to work in the studio of Arturo Prins and Oskar Ranzenhofer, and learns there the two things a foreign architect cannot bring in a trunk: the municipal codes, and who commissions what. The studio is drawing a neo-Gothic pile for the Faculty of Law, all pinnacle and pointed arch, and Palanti puts his hand to it. No source records the address of the office or the day he walks out of it. The city he is learning to build in is barely older, as a metropolis, than he is.
stops.quote: lavorò in primo luogo nello studio di Arturo Prins ed Oskar Ranzenhofer
suggested_refs: The Prins and Ranzenhofer practice, Buenos Aires, address unrecorded

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the Italian Pavilion of the Centenario
stops.date_confidence: the Railway and Land Transport exposition is inaugurated 17 July 1910 per es.wikipedia, 'Exposición Internacional del Centenario', which places it 'en los predios del Regimiento 1 de Patricios'; Palanti's work on its Italian Pavilion is attested by es.wikipedia's work list without a date. The pin is reconstructed to the Patricios barracks grounds in Palermo and is not documented at street level; the research pool's Palermo park coordinate belonged to the Agriculture and Industry sections and has been dropped
stops.campa: Argentina turns a hundred and builds an exposition to say so, spread across the capital in sections: agriculture and industry out at Palermo, railways and land transport on the Patricios regiment's grounds. Palanti works the Italian Pavilion there, alongside the architect Francisco Gianotti. It is a building meant to be taken down, and it is taken down, and it is the whole reason he is in the country at all. Nothing of it stands, and no source reached here gives its plan, its cost or a photograph of it.
stops.quote: en los predios del Regimiento 1 de Patricios
suggested_refs: The Italian Pavilion of the 1910 Ferrocarriles y Transportes Terrestres exposition, demolished

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the neo-Gothic Faculty of Law
stops.date_confidence: year attested by es.wikipedia's work list; month and day unknown and defaulted to 01 January. The identification of the commission with the neo-Gothic building at Av. Gral. Las Heras 2214, now the UBA Facultad de Ingeniería, comes from it.wikipedia; the coordinate is OSM way 18613538 and corrects the research pool's pin by about 1.6 km
stops.campa: The Faculty of Law rises on Las Heras as a neo-Gothic cathedral of jurisprudence, drawn inside the Prins and Ranzenhofer studio with Palanti collaborating. It is never finished as a law faculty. The building stands and the engineers take it: pointed windows, buttresses, a nave without a chancel, lecture halls where the choir would be. Palanti is twenty-six and detailing another man's cathedral. Eight years later he starts one of his own on the Avenida de Mayo and cuts the ornament for it himself.
stops.quote: un edificio simbolo dello stile neogotico
stops.quote_source: it.wikipedia, 'Mario Palanti', on the Facultad de Derecho commission
suggested_refs: The unfinished neo-Gothic Facultad de Derecho, Av. Gral. Las Heras 2214, now the Facultad de Ingeniería

stops.name: Avenida Rivadavia 1916, the Building of the Atlantes
stops.date_confidence: year attested by es.wikipedia's work list; month and day unknown and defaulted to 01 January. The coordinate is Av. Rivadavia 1916 per OSM way 265311278 and corrects the research pool's pin by about 900 m; the pool's coordinate landed in Monserrat, six blocks east of the building
stops.campa: On Avenida Rivadavia he raises the Edificio de los Atlantes, its balconies carried on the shoulders of stone men straining upward out of the facade, the Renaissance Revival vocabulary he keeps for Italian money. The same year he draws residential blocks and the Cinema Presidente Roca on the same avenue. Julio Argentino Roca, twice president, dies that October and goes into the ground at Recoleta; the cinema carrying his name opens under the hand of an architect who landed five years after his last term.
suggested_refs: The telamones of the Edificio de los Atlantes, Av. Rivadavia 1916, Balvanera

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the Grimoldi chalet
stops.date_confidence: year attested by es.wikipedia's work list, which also records the demolition; month and day unknown and defaulted to 01 January. No address survives, so the coordinate is the canonical Buenos Aires pin standing for the city
stops.campa: He builds the Grimoldi chalet, a house for a family in a city inventing a suburban idiom out of imported parts. It is demolished; the sources keep the name and lose the address, and nothing of it can now be stood in front of. It belongs to the long first list of his Buenos Aires work, the Costaguta residence, the Cassotana rental block, the cinema, the apartment houses, all of it drawn before the tower and remembered by almost nobody since. Italy enters the war in May and he goes back to it in uniform.
suggested_refs: The demolished Grimoldi chalet, Buenos Aires, address unrecorded

stops.name: Trentino front, the lieutenant of engineers
stops.date_confidence: the service is attested by it.wikipedia: lieutenant of the Genio militare on the Trentino front, 1915 to the end of the war. His sector is named by no reachable source. The pin is the Asiago plateau, a principal engineering theatre of that front, and is an explicit reconstruction; month and day defaulted to 01 January
stops.campa: Italy enters the war and Palanti goes back into it, a lieutenant of the Genio militare on the Trentino front, where the engineering corps does the work that artillery and rock make necessary: galleries, cable ways, roads cut into limestone, positions blasted at two thousand metres. The corps runs on men who know how a load moves through stone, and he is one of them. Three and a half years of it, and no reachable source names the sector he holds or a single work he signs there.
suggested_refs: The Genio militare works of the Asiago plateau, standing here for an unnamed sector

stops.name: Italy, the armistice
stops.date_confidence: it.wikipedia attests only that his service runs to the end of the First World War. 4 November 1918 is the date the Villa Giusti armistice takes effect on the Italian front; it is not attested for Palanti, and his whereabouts on that day are unknown. The pin is the generic Milan coordinate, a placement and not a location
stops.campa: The armistice signed at Villa Giusti takes effect on the fourth of November and the Italian front stops. Palanti's service runs to the end of the war; nothing records where he stands when it ends, or what he has built in three years, or whether the Brussels medal and the Buenos Aires commissions still mean anything to him. He is thirty-three. The country he has been defending will spend four years arguing about what it won, and the country he has been building in has grown rich selling beef to both sides.
suggested_refs: The armistice of Villa Giusti, 3 November 1918, effective 4 November

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the practice resumed
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, not attestation: no reachable source records the discharge, the voyage, or a 1919 return to Buenos Aires. The year is inferred backwards from the attested start of Barolo construction, which en.wikipedia's infobox gives as 1919. The pin is the canonical Buenos Aires coordinate inherited byte-identically from victoria_ocampo.journey.json
stops.campa: He is back on the Avenida de Mayo, working for himself, and the commission of his life is waiting. Luis Barolo, a textile industrialist out of Lombardy who has made a fortune in Argentine cotton, wants an office building. He also wants something an Argentine architect could not give him, which is why he asks an Italian: a monument to Dante Alighieri, on the grandest avenue of a city seven thousand miles from Florence, in a country whose Italians land by the hundred thousand and have nothing here older than themselves.
suggested_refs: Luis Barolo, textile industrialist of Lombard origin, patron of the tower

stops.name: Avenida de Mayo 1370, the Barolo begun
stops.date_confidence: construction start attested as 1919 by en.wikipedia's infobox, with es.wikipedia giving the fuller span 1919-1923; month and day unknown and defaulted to 01 January. Coordinate taken from the en.wikipedia coord template for the Palacio Barolo, 34 36 34.4 S 58 23 9.1 W, and used byte-identically at every Barolo stop; the research pool's geography lens gave a pin about 330 m east and disagreed with its own afterlife lens
stops.campa: Work begins on the Palacio Barolo. Palanti sets the Divine Comedy into the structure itself: a hundred metres of height for the hundred cantos, twenty-two floors, the basement and ground floor as Inferno with nine vaulted bays for the nine circles, floors one to fourteen as Purgatorio, fifteen to twenty-two as Paradiso, and a lighthouse on the crown. Dante climbed it walking behind Virgil. Palanti builds it as a stair, so that a clerk going up to his office comes out of hell every morning at nine.
stops.quote: The lighthouse at the top of the building can be seen all the way in Montevideo
suggested_refs: The nine vaulted bays and Latin inscriptions of the Barolo entrance passage
Dante's hundred cantos, the building's unit of measure

stops.name: Plaza Independencia, the Salvo brothers buy the Giralda plot
stops.date_confidence: the purchase of the La Giralda plot by the Salvo brothers and the commission to Palanti are attested by it.wikipedia, 'Palazzo Salvo'; the year is given without month or day, defaulted to 01 January. The coordinate matches the en.wikipedia coord for the Palacio Salvo exactly and is used byte-identically at every Salvo stop; the research pool carried three mutually inconsistent Montevideo pins
stops.campa: Across the estuary in Montevideo three Uruguayan brothers of Italian descent, Angel and Jose and Lorenzo Salvo, buy the corner of Plaza Independencia where the confectionery La Giralda stands, the room in which a tango called La cumparsita was first played two years before. They want a luxury hotel and they want the Milanese who is building the Barolo. Palanti agrees to draw them a twin, and the two towers begin to face each other across ninety miles of brown water.
suggested_refs: The confectionery La Giralda, Plaza Independencia, where La cumparsita premiered in 1917

stops.name: Avenida Santa Fe and Callao, the Roccatagliata building
stops.date_confidence: year attested by en.wikipedia's work list; month and day unknown and defaulted to 01 January. Location taken from it.wikipedia, which places the Edificio Roccatagliata at Avenida Santa Fe and Avenida Callao; the coordinate is the Callao 1201 geocode and corrects the research pool's pin by about 1.9 km, the pool having placed it in Monserrat
stops.campa: At the crossing of Santa Fe and Callao he puts up the Edificio Roccatagliata for another of the Italian commercial families, Renaissance Revival again, stone and cornice and a corner turned with ceremony. It is the ordinary business of the practice while the extraordinary thing rises twenty blocks south. He is thirty-five and the Barolo is three years from opening. The Buenos Aires he assembles out of stone and cornice photographs as Europe to anyone who cannot read the street signs, and the men paying for it left Europe to get here.
suggested_refs: The Edificio Roccatagliata at Avenida Santa Fe and Avenida Callao, Barrio Norte

stops.name: Avenida de Mayo 1370, the Barolo opens
stops.date_confidence: completion attested to the year by en.wikipedia and es.wikipedia; month and day unknown and defaulted to 01 January. La Nacion's centenary article of 7 July 2023 suggests a July inauguration, which no source states and which is not adopted here. Correction carried: the building is the tallest in South America only until the Palacio Salvo of 1928, and the tallest in Buenos Aires until the Kavanagh of 1935 or 1936; the research pool's claim of a South American record held to the Kavanagh is contradicted by es.wikipedia and it.wikipedia
stops.campa: The Palacio Barolo opens, a hundred metres of reinforced concrete and Lombard-Gothic ornament, the tallest building in South America and the tallest in Buenos Aires for a dozen years after that. The beacon at the summit stands for the nine choirs of angels and throws its light across the river toward Montevideo. Marcelo Torcuato de Alvear is president. Victoria Ocampo, reading the Comedy as private confession since 1908, publishes De Francesca a Beatrice the following year in Madrid.
stops.quote_source: La Nacion, Silvina Vitale, 'Cumple 100 anos: cuales son los secretos y misterios que esconde uno de los edificios mas iconicos', 7 July 2023. Low confidence: two fetches of the same article disagreed on whether the phrase belongs to the heritage historian Leonel Contreras or is unattributed, and it is said about Palanti, not by him
suggested_refs: The Barolo beacon, an arc lamp of 300,000 candelas, for the nine choirs of angels
Victoria Ocampo, De Francesca a Beatrice, Madrid, 1924

stops.name: Plaza Independencia, the cornerstone of the Salvo
stops.date_confidence: it.wikipedia dates the cornerstone to 1923; es.wikipedia and it.wikipedia date the design or commission to 1922; en.wikipedia dates construction start to 1925. Three dates from three sources, probably a design date, a cornerstone and a construction start, but no source reconciles them and they are left standing. Month and day defaulted to 01 January
stops.campa: The cornerstone of the Palacio Salvo goes down in Montevideo in the same year the Barolo opens. Palanti has designed the pair to answer each other, two lit spires at either end of the Rio de la Plata, and the tradition that grows around them holds that he meant the two beams to meet over the water and that an error of calculation kept them apart. What the sources do carry is the intention: one monument in two countries, drawn by one hand, paid for by two sets of Italian money that crossed on the same ships.
suggested_refs: The legend of the bridge of light between Barolo and Salvo, recorded by es.wikipedia as legend

segments.name: Rome, the Mole, and the Tomb

stops.name: Rome, Palazzo Chigi, the Mole Littoria offered
stops.date_confidence: year attested by it.wikipedia, which also confirms the city, the tower being intended 'in Roma', and the rejection after Piacentini's criticism. The venue is reconstructed: no source names the room or the meeting. Palazzo Chigi is Mussolini's seat of government at that date and stands here as a guess; the coordinate is OSM relation 325553 and corrects the research pool's pin by about 195 m. Month and day defaulted to 01 January
stops.campa: Palanti brings to Mussolini's government a project called the Mole Littoria: eighty-eight storeys, three hundred and thirty-five metres, a fascist tower for Rome taller than anything then standing on earth. He has just proved in Buenos Aires that he can build the tallest thing on a continent. Marcello Piacentini, who will own Roman architecture for the next twenty years, criticises it and the Mole is abandoned. Gabriele D'Annunzio had held Fiume through the same years Palanti was raising the Barolo.
suggested_refs: Palanti, L'Eternale: mole littoria - Roma MCMXXVI (1926), the project published after its refusal

stops.name: Cimitero Monumentale di Milano, the tomb for his parents
stops.date_confidence: it.wikipedia, 'Civico Mausoleo Palanti', dates construction 1924-1928 and inauguration 1929, and corrects the research pool on two points: the aedicule was designed as a tomb for his parents, not for himself, and it was not called the Civico Mausoleo until 1981. Month and day defaulted to 01 January. Coordinate note: the pool's two lenses disagree by about 280 m for this tomb; 45.4842/9.1783 sits at the Famedio entrance rather than at Riparto V, and no plot-level coordinate is published
stops.campa: At the Cimitero Monumentale of Milan he begins a funerary aedicule for Giovanni and Virginia Palanti, the carpenter and the dressmaker, in rose granite from Baveno, Riparto V, Edicola 83. He is at the height of his South American practice, drawing two skyscrapers on two shores, and what he draws for his own family is a temple the size of a room. Over the threshold he cuts the reason in capitals. It takes four years to build and he is fifty-four years from lying in it himself.
stops.quote: PER ETERNARE LA MEMORIA DE'MIEI CARI GENITORI HO ERETTO QUESTO TEMPIO
stops.quote_source: Threshold inscription of the Edicola Palanti, Cimitero Monumentale di Milano, quoted by it.wikipedia, 'Civico Mausoleo Palanti'
suggested_refs: The Edicola Palanti in rose granite of Baveno, Riparto V, Edicola 83

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the Uboldi building
stops.date_confidence: year attested by en.wikipedia's work list; month and day unknown and defaulted to 01 January. No address is given by any reachable source, so the coordinate is the canonical Buenos Aires pin standing for the city
stops.campa: The Uboldi building goes up in Buenos Aires, one more block for one more Italian family, drawn in the same year he offers Mussolini a tower for Rome and buries his parents' memory in Milanese granite. In one year his name goes on a Buenos Aires apartment block, a Roman skyscraper project and a Milanese tomb. Jorge Luis Borges, twenty-five and lately back from Geneva, walks these streets and will spend sixty years writing about Dante in a city where Dante already stands a hundred metres high on the Avenida de Mayo.
suggested_refs: Borges, Nueve ensayos dantescos, and the Dante of Buenos Aires

stops.name: Rome, the Commendatore and the Fondazione Palanti
stops.date_confidence: the date is that of Regio Decreto 12 maggio 1927 n. 999, printed in the Gazzetta Ufficiale of 6 July 1927 and cited by it.wikipedia's honours section, which styles him comm. Mario Palanti. It is a decree date, not a ceremony date; no reachable source dates the conferral of the Commendatore rank or the two academy memberships, and this decree fixes only a terminus ante quem. The pin is the Accademia dei Virtuosi seat at the Pantheon and stands for his Roman affiliations; the Regia scuola d'architettura named in the decree has no reachable 1927 address
stops.campa: A royal decree establishes the Fondazione Mario Palanti at the Regia scuola d'architettura in Rome and authorises it to accept two donations from him. The Gazzetta Ufficiale prints the decree in July and calls him comm. Mario Palanti; he already holds the Commendatore rank in the Order of the Crown of Italy and sits as an academician of San Luca and of the Virtuosi al Pantheon. Rome will not let him build the Mole and will not stop decorating him. What the two donations to the school consisted of, no reachable source says.
stops.quote_source: Regio Decreto 12 maggio 1927 n. 999, Gazzetta Ufficiale, 6 July 1927, cited by it.wikipedia, 'Mario Palanti'
suggested_refs: The Fondazione Mario Palanti at the Regia scuola d'architettura, Rome, 1927

segments.name: The Twin on the Other Bank

stops.name: Plaza Independencia, the Salvo rising
stops.date_confidence: construction start attested as 1925 by en.wikipedia, 'Palacio Salvo', against the 1923 cornerstone of it.wikipedia; month and day unknown and defaulted to 01 January. The twenty-seven floors and the height of 105 m to the tip come from it.wikipedia and es.wikipedia
stops.campa: Construction proper begins on the Palacio Salvo, twenty-seven floors going up over Plaza Independencia in a fusion nobody has a name for: Art Deco massing, Gothic detail, a Neoclassical base, and a tower on top like a lighthouse that has climbed out of the sea. The hotel the Salvo brothers commissioned will never really be a hotel. It becomes offices and apartments, and in the end a museum of tango standing on the floor where La cumparsita was first played.
suggested_refs: The Museo del Tango de Montevideo on the Salvo ground floor, in the room of La Giralda

stops.name: Paysandu, the Tienda London Paris
stops.date_confidence: attested by name and year in es.wikipedia's Palanti work list; month and day unknown and defaulted to 01 January. The research pool wrongly recorded this commission as unnamed and undated. No address is given, so the pin is the town of Paysandu
stops.campa: Two hundred and fifty miles up the Uruguay river from Montevideo, at Paysandu on the western frontier, Palanti draws a department store: the Tienda London Paris. It is the only commission recorded outside the two capitals, a piece of metropolitan facade set down in a river town of tanneries and cattle boats. The architect of the Barolo, with the Salvo half-built behind him down the estuary, is also for one year the architect of a provincial shop counter, and the sources keep the name and nothing else.
suggested_refs: The Tienda London Paris department store, Paysandu, address unrecorded

stops.name: Barrio Parque, the Palacio Automotor projected
stops.date_confidence: es.wikipedia, 'Palacio Alcorta', dates the project to 1927 and the inauguration to 1 December 1928; the research pool logged this as an unresolved 1927 against 1928 discrepancy, which it is not, and the two dates are carried here as two stops. Month and day of the project defaulted to 01 January. Coordinate is OSM relation 12403783 and corrects the pool's pin by about 400 m
stops.campa: He draws the Palacio Automotor for the Resta brothers, Chrysler dealers, in Barrio Parque: a showroom for motor cars with a test track on the roof, promoted as the first palace-autodrome anywhere. Historicist stone below, an oval of banked concrete above, cars driven up through the building to run in the open air over Palermo. Le Corbusier, who will lecture in this city in two years and has no use for its historicism, is drawing his own roof decks in Paris that season.
stops.quote: El edificio fue proyectado originalmente en 1927 por el arquitecto italiano Mario Palanti
suggested_refs: The Estadio Olimpo rooftop test track of the Palacio Alcorta

stops.name: Avenida de Mayo 1152, the Hotel Excelsior
stops.date_confidence: es.wikipedia gives the span 1927-1928 and it.wikipedia lists '1927/8: Hotel Excelsior'; en.wikipedia dates the Hotel Castelar to 1928. Month and day defaulted to 01 January. Coordinate is OSM way 476772574 and corrects the pool's pin by about 200 m. The pool's association of the hotel with Federico Garcia Lorca is unsourced in the consulted pages and has been dropped rather than hedged
stops.campa: One block along the avenue from the Barolo he builds the Hotel Excelsior, a European hotel for a city that wants to be told it is European, renamed the Castelar later. It takes two years. Palanti has now signed both ends of the same stretch of the Avenida de Mayo, the boulevard cut through Buenos Aires in imitation of Madrid and Paris. Two hundred metres up the same pavement the tower with the beacon on it is four years old, and both buildings carry his name.
suggested_refs: The Hotel Castelar, Avenida de Mayo 1152, opened as the Excelsior

stops.name: Plaza Independencia, the Salvo inaugurated
stops.date_confidence: year attested by en.wikipedia and it.wikipedia; month and day unknown and defaulted to 01 January. The Latin American height record from 1928 to 1935 is it.wikipedia's, and it is the fact that corrects the research pool's claim for the Barolo
stops.campa: The Palacio Salvo is inaugurated, a hundred and five metres to the tip, the tallest building in Latin America, five years after its twin across the water. Palanti is forty-three and has built the two tallest buildings in Latin America, one in each of two countries, neither of them his own. The Barolo beacon and the Salvo crown now stand lit at either end of the estuary, and en.wikipedia records that the Barolo light carries as far as Montevideo. Nine years lie between the two cornerstones, and he draws no third tower.
stops.quote: Dalla sua inaugurazione al 1935 ... il Palazzo Salvo fu il piu alto edificio dell'America Latina
suggested_refs: The Salvo dome and its original lighthouse, specified by Palanti and removed at an unrecorded date

stops.name: Barrio Parque, the Palacio Alcorta opens
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by es.wikipedia, 'Palacio Alcorta'
stops.campa: On the first of December the Palacio Alcorta opens on Figueroa Alcorta, its rooftop circuit named the Estadio Olimpo, cars climbing through a stone palace to race above the treetops of Palermo. It is the last large thing he finishes in Argentina. Nineteen years after landing to put up a temporary pavilion he has given the city a Dante skyscraper, a hotel, a cinema, apartment blocks, a false cathedral of law, and a garage with a racetrack on the roof, and he is two years from leaving.
stops.quote: El edificio fue inaugurado el 1 de diciembre de 1928.
suggested_refs: The Resta brothers' Chrysler dealership and the first palace-autodrome

stops.name: Cimitero Monumentale di Milano, the Edicola inaugurated
stops.date_confidence: inauguration attested to the year by it.wikipedia, 'Civico Mausoleo Palanti', which reads the year off the relief on the rear face: MCMXXIX, anno VII. Month and day unknown and defaulted to 01 January. Whether Palanti attended is a gap: no source records his presence in Milan at any point between 1924 and 1930
stops.campa: The aedicule at the Monumentale is finished and inaugurated, the year cut in relief on its rear face as MCMXXIX, anno VII of the fascist era. Rose granite, a temple front, his parents inside. Palanti has built for the Barolos and the Salvos and the Uboldis, families who bought their monuments; this one he pays for himself, and it is the only building of his standing in the city where he was born and trained. Whether he is there to see it opened, no source says.
suggested_refs: The MCMXXIX relief and the fascist year VII on the rear face of the Edicola Palanti

stops.name: Puerto Madero, the last sailing
stops.date_confidence: year attested by en.wikipedia: he leaves Argentina and returns to live in Italy in 1930. Port, vessel and date of sailing are unrecorded, as at his arrival; month and day defaulted to 01 January. The pin is the Puerto Madero docks and is a reconstruction of the point of departure
stops.campa: He leaves the River Plate for good and goes home to Milan, twenty-one years after coming ashore. He is forty-five. Behind him on the two banks stand the two towers, already too tall and too strange for the modernism arriving to replace them; Le Corbusier lectured here the previous October and Hermann Keyserling three months before that, both received at Victoria Ocampo's house at San Isidro. Claude Levi-Strauss may touch this same port in five years, going south.
suggested_refs: Villa Ocampo, San Isidro, hinge of the 1929 European visits to the Plate

stops.name: Milan, the Palandomus patent
stops.date_confidence: it.wikipedia dates the Palandomus to the turn of the 1920s and 1930s, which means it was begun while he was still working in South America; the research pool's '1930s, back in Milan' framing is wrong on both counts. The exact patent date is a gap. Month and day defaulted to 01 January
stops.campa: Across the turn of the decade he designs and patents a system for putting up buildings dry, without mortar, and calls it the Palandomus. The man who spent twenty years cutting telamones and Gothic vaults into reinforced concrete now wants houses assembled like furniture. No source names a building put up with it, or the patent number, or the year the patent was granted. The Palandomus survives as one line in one Italian encyclopaedia article, and the two towers survive as a century of photographs.
stops.quote: A cavallo degli anni '20-'30 progetto un sistema, brevettato, per erigere costruzioni a secco: il Palandomus
suggested_refs: The Palandomus dry-construction patent, date and holdings unrecorded

stops.name: Milano Centrale, the ramps
stops.date_confidence: year attested by it.wikipedia; month and day unknown and defaulted to 01 January. Milan is under Allied bombing from 1940 onward, with the heaviest raids in 1942 and 1943; the bombing is context, not a dated event attached to Palanti
stops.campa: He designs the ramps at Milano Centrale, the enormous station Ulisse Stacchini finished a decade earlier, all stone eagles and vaults of glass. It is a small late commission in a city under bombing, and it is the last work of his that gets built. Palanti is fifty-seven. The two tallest buildings in South America are his, and in his own country he is fitting an approach road to somebody else's terminus while the roof over it waits to be broken from the air.
suggested_refs: Ulisse Stacchini's Milano Centrale, 1931, to which Palanti added the ramps

stops.name: Milan, the marriage to Nahir Marazzi Castiglioni
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by it.wikipedia. No church, registry or witness is named by any reachable source, and the pin is the generic Milan coordinate standing for the city
stops.campa: On the seventh of January, in a Milan that has been bombed and will be bombed again, Mario Palanti marries Nahir Marazzi Castiglioni. He is fifty-seven. There is no record of a church, or of who stands with them, or of how the two of them met. He has thirty-five years still to live and will build nothing of any size in either hemisphere again. In Buenos Aires the Kavanagh has stood taller than the Barolo for seven years; in Montevideo the Salvo still tops the plaza; and their architect is a married man in a blacked-out flat.
suggested_refs: Nahir Marazzi Castiglioni, married 7 January 1943, otherwise undocumented

stops.name: Cimitero Monumentale di Milano, the Edicola given to the city
stops.date_confidence: year attested by it.wikipedia, 'Civico Mausoleo Palanti': Palanti donates the Edicola to the Comune di Milano in 1974. Month and day unknown and defaulted to 01 January
stops.campa: At eighty-nine he makes over the aedicule at the Monumentale to the Comune di Milano. The tomb built for a carpenter and a dressmaker passes into the keeping of the city, which will look after the granite in exchange for the right to lay others in it. He has outlived the fascist era whose calendar is carved on the back of the building, and he has outlived the men who commissioned him on both banks of the Plate. No building of his has gone up anywhere since the ramps at Milano Centrale in 1942. He has four years left.
suggested_refs: The 1974 donation of the Edicola Palanti to the Comune di Milano

stops.name: Milan, the death
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by en.wikipedia and it.wikipedia. Contradiction recorded and not resolved: es.wikipedia hedges the year as '4 de septiembre de 1978 o 4 de septiembre de 1979'. Neither figure has been checked against a registry
stops.campa: Mario Palanti dies in Milan on the fourth of September, sixteen days short of ninety-three. He was born in this city, trained in it, and spent the twenty-one central years of his life on the other side of the Atlantic building the two objects anybody remembers. The Milanese papers of 1978 have little reason to make much of the death of an eclectic from before the war. In Buenos Aires the beacon he set over the Avenida de Mayo is dark, and will be relit thirty-one years after him.
stops.quote: 4 de septiembre de 1978 o 4 de septiembre de 1979
stops.quote_source: es.wikipedia, 'Mario Palanti', recording the unresolved death year
suggested_refs: The disputed death year, 1978 in en and it Wikipedia, 1978 or 1979 in es

stops.name: Cimitero Monumentale di Milano, the burial
stops.date_confidence: gap: no reachable source gives the day of the burial, only the year and the place. Month and day are defaulted to 01 January rather than invented for September, though the burial necessarily follows the death of 4 September. The tomb is named here as the Edicola Palanti, not the Civico Mausoleo, which it does not become until 1981
stops.campa: He is laid in the Edicola Palanti at Riparto V, the temple he raised for his parents fifty years earlier while his draughtsmen in Buenos Aires were inking a tower a hundred metres high. Milan to the Avenida de Mayo is eleven thousand kilometres. He drew this tomb while the two skyscrapers were still on the board, and came back to it fifty-four years later. The granite is the same rose Baveno he chose then, and no source records the day of the burial or who attended.

stops.name: Cimitero Monumentale di Milano, the tomb renamed
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by it.wikipedia, 'Civico Mausoleo Palanti': the Edicola is officially renamed on 4 February 1981, three years after the burial and seven after the donation
stops.campa: On the fourth of February the Comune formally renames the aedicule the Civico Mausoleo Palanti. What was a family tomb becomes a civic one, and the architect's name, which in Italy had attached to nothing standing, attaches at last to a building in Milan: his own grave. Elsewhere it is on two skylines and on nothing else. The Mole Littoria was refused, the Palazzo del Littorio project was never built, and the ramps at Centrale carry traffic under another man's roof.
suggested_refs: The official renaming of 4 February 1981

stops.name: Plaza Independencia, the Salvo declared a national monument
stops.date_confidence: year attested by en.wikipedia, 'Palacio Salvo'; month and day unknown and defaulted to 01 January. The Uruguayan instrument itself was not read
stops.campa: Uruguay declares the Palacio Salvo a National Historic Monument. The luxury hotel that was never a hotel, the tower Montevideo spent seventy years calling ugly and then could not imagine the plaza without, becomes protected fabric. On the ground floor, where the confectionery La Giralda stood and a tango was first played in 1917, a museum of tango will open. No one planned that. The Uruguayan instrument of declaration was not read for this file, and what it protects, and what it leaves unprotected, is not established here.
suggested_refs: The Uruguayan national monument declaration of 1996

stops.name: Avenida de Mayo 1370, the Barolo declared a national monument
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by es.wikipedia, which states it twice and cites Decreto 437/97 at infoleg.gov.ar; en.wikipedia's body text agrees. Month and day defaulted to 01 January; the decree itself was not read
stops.campa: By Decreto 437 the Palacio Barolo becomes a National Historic Monument of Argentina, seventy-four years after it opened and nineteen after its architect died. The Dante scheme has by then become the thing the building is for: the nine bays, the twenty-two floors, the spire that lines up with the Southern Cross on the ninth of July. Jorge Luis Borges, who published Nueve ensayos dantescos in 1982 and died in Geneva four years later, had walked past it his whole life.

stops.name: Avenida de Mayo 1370, the Bicentennial Lighthouse
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by es.wikipedia: the beacon returns on 25 September 2009 and burns for half an hour on the 25th of each month until 25 May 2010. The research pool's 'lit nightly' is wrong and has been corrected against the same source
stops.campa: The beacon on the Barolo is lit again after decades of darkness, a five thousand watt lamp in place of the original arc of three hundred thousand candelas, and named the Faro del Bicentenario. It burns for half an hour on the twenty-fifth of each month until the twenty-fifth of May 2010, when Argentina turns two hundred: the same anniversary whose hundredth Palanti crossed an ocean to help celebrate, with a pavilion that was taken down as soon as the crowds went home.

stops.campa: A new light goes up on the Salvo dome, LED where there had been a television antenna, and before the antenna the lighthouse Palanti specified and nobody wrote down the removal of. The Gran Salvo crown burns over Plaza Independencia again. Ninety-four years after the cornerstone both towers stand lit on their two banks, and the beams still do not meet over the water; the calculation that was supposed to join them, if it was ever made, has never been found.
